title: Transfer task: plan and begin
target: Organize the given measurements and details. Begin your own position prediction.
criteria: Organize the task data with fixed axes and matching units.
Calculate central and bounded final coordinates.
Save an explicit plan for the graph and explanation.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A simplified tracking calculation uses east as +x and north as +y. Distance is in km and time is in seconds. Which velocity units can you use directly?
cpa.guide: Velocity must use the same length and time units as the coordinate equation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A probe begins 40 km west and 6 km north of the origin. What are initial coordinates with east +x and north +y?
cpa.guide: West is negative x; north is positive y.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A toy probe starts at (−40, 6) km with constant velocity (+3, −0.5) km/s for 8 s. What is final position?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Initial x is exactly −40 km; vx is between 2.8 and 3.2 km/s; t = 8 s exactly. What are final x bounds?
cpa.guide: Apply x_f = −40 + vx(8) to each endpoint.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which plan would make a constant-velocity prediction reviewable?
options: Save givens, axes, units, equations, endpoint calculations, and a graph plan with assumptions.
Save only an unlabeled final number.
Save a claim that all future motion is known.
cpa.guide: A traceable plan lets another person check the reasoning and representation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A simple prediction uses a straight path and treats Earth as still. It leaves out gravity and Earth’s motion. What should you do next before saying whether a real object will come near Earth?
options: Treat the toy endpoint as a confirmed collision forecast.
Add the missing dynamics and compare both bodies at matching times with uncertainty.
Use only whether x becomes positive.
cpa.guide: The simplified exercise cannot establish a real encounter without additional modeling.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
